narr: Multiple mesoscale convective vortices (MCVs) were seen across Arizona during the morning. Clearing skies allowed for daytime heating to add to the already unstable atmosphere. As a result, there were multiple flash floods across the area.
ev: Flooding was reported in rural Steamboat Canyon. Water washed out a residential road.
Flash flooding was reported on the north side of Tuba City washed away dirt roads and people had to be rescued from the water.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline Fire scar (2022) resulted in 1-2 feet of water flowing in Schultz Creek, over Mount Elden Road, and overwhelming the culvert at Highway 180, and flowing onto the bike path next to Highway 180. The water flowing over the highway caused a temporary closure.
A swift water rescue took place along Indian Route 4 by Burnt Corn Wash (about 5 miles east of Pi��on) where an elderly gentleman in his car was rescued.
Flash flooding unearthed two main water pipelines (8 and 10 inch) which had to be shut down. This left around 75 people with out flowing water in Indian Wells, Dilkon, and Seba areas.
Flash flooding was reported over Highway 98 five miles east of K'ai'bii'to. Some roads washed out in the area.
